entries.test: Published analyses of language models available in June 2022 could establish whether they encoded stable world representations beyond their next-word prediction objective.
entries.note: The proposition preserves the authors' epistemic qualification; next-word prediction alone does not establish the absence of world representations.
This evaluates the difficulty of a research direction and recommends prioritizing it.

entries.test: Public research histories, funding allocations, and documented project decisions could show whether prioritizing word prediction displaced work on theories of cognitive models through June 2022.
entries.note: The authors suggest an actual research tradeoff, which can be investigated through historical evidence.

entries.test: Controlled evaluations of June 2022 models' ability to distinguish truth from falsehood, together with interventions adding reference and cognitive models, could test the asserted incapacity and its cause.
entries.note: Read in context, this concerns then-current models and their ability to assess factual plausibility.

entries.test: Public architecture analyses and reproducible demonstrations could establish whether June 2022 systems represented relevant world facts and used them to identify and demonstrate errors in their own answers.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supplies a practical reading of proving oneself wrong: assessing and rejecting an erroneous assertion.
The authors mock a belief; they do not endorse the embedded optimistic prediction or state a definite contrary forecast.

entries.test: The authors' published experimental outputs or representative replications using the contemporary DALL-E Mini version and quoted prompt could establish the reported action and food-assignment failure rates.
entries.note: These are concrete claims about visible image outputs for a specified prompt.
The asserted necessity of large-scale learning is explicitly qualified by 'almost certainly'.

entries.test: Public analyses and controlled probing of the contemporary networks could establish whether their internal states linked linguistic expressions to referents and dynamically updated representations of entities and relationships.
entries.note: The substantive claim concerns representational properties; 'pretty' is an incidental aesthetic judgment.
